Logs show what happened, but not why it was allowed. TraceMem is an attempt to make decision context durable. Meta's multi-billion dollar acquisition of Manus reflects its confidence in the evolution of "intelligent capability" from "brain-only" to "brain-and-hand" proficiency. IT veteran Li Guoping commented on Manus's change of ownership, noting that the "intelligent capability" refers to the composite ability of agents in cognition and execution. In his view, the SaaS industry is also undergoing its own intelligent transformation—"If SaaS continues to rely mainly on human-system (interface) interaction without embracing intelligent transformation, it will inevitably be overturned by the times." The fundamental shift in human-computer interaction models represents a disruptive change brought by the Agent wave to the SaaS industry.

This perspective stems from Li Guoping's decades of firsthand experience with transformative moments: in the software era, operating systems were the core of the digital world; in the PC internet era, portals and later search engines became the gateways to the digital world; in the mobile internet era, apps took over as the entry point; and in the cloud computing era, SaaS integrated and encapsulated all capabilities. Li Guoping, who worked at Microsoft for over a decade, currently serves as the Dean of the Digital Economy and Fintech Research Institute at Baiwang Co., Ltd., a leading domestic tax and finance SaaS provider. Over the nearly 20 years since the rise of cloud computing, he has consistently embraced and adopted new technological waves.

Where will the future of SaaS head under the Agent wave? In Li Guoping's view, SaaS is unlikely to disappear within the next five years but will first transition toward embedded, localized intelligent applications.

excerpt_i18n.en: If your impression of AI is still confined to dialog boxes on your phone screen, or just having it draw pictures or write poetry, then a 3D printer at the Creality booth at China's first smart hardware exhibition of 2026 might just change your perception. In the 5,000+ square meter exhibition area, Creality's new product, the SPARKX i7, became the star attraction. Many visitors gathered around this small machine that was "creating objects out of thin air" and marveled: "I used to think 3D printing was a toy for geeks with a high barrier to entry, but looking at this operation now, it seems as simple as ordering takeout." This is precisely the message Creality aims to convey with the SPARKX i7: the "iPhone moment" for 3D printing has truly arrived. The SPARKX i7 is intelligent and user-friendly, lowering the barrier to entry. Many people unfamiliar with 3D printers might ask: "I don’t know how to model or adjust parameters—can I still use 3D printing?" In the past, operating a 3D printer was indeed like driving a manual race car, requiring manual leveling and slicing, where a single misstep could easily lead to failure. But the SPARKX i7 is like an "automatic" family car equipped with assisted driving features.

Hosted by Alibaba Cloud, this exhibition brought together over 220 companies and 1,500 smart hardware products, and is regarded by the industry as a new core venue for observing trends in Chinese AI hardware. 7. Aima reportedly conducted massive layoffs, with some departments cutting 50% of staff; compensation is only one month's salary! Official response.
8. Meta responded to rumors of 17.5 million Instagram account data leaks: The system was not breached, and user accounts are secure.
